status_note: active, maintained by Frappe (powers frappe.io); requires Frappe Framework v15-17 bench; recently added a full server-side AI agent ('Bob') via litellm
core_problem: A Figma-like visual website builder inside the Frappe framework that stores pages as a JSON block tree, renders them server-side to lean HTML/CSS (Lighthouse-friendly), supports components with version pinning, data-bound/repeater blocks, per-breakpoint styles, one-click publish with snapshots, and (new) an AI agent that edits the same block tree through validated tool calls.
architecture: Python app (builder/) + Vue 3 frontend (frontend/). DATA MODEL: a Builder Page doctype (builder/builder/doctype/builder_page/builder_page.json) holds `blocks` (Long Text JSON, the published tree) and `draft_blocks` (working tree), plus route, published/staging flags, page_data_script (Python), dynamic_route, client_scripts, head/body HTML, meta fields, is_standard/app for export-to-app. Each block (frontend/src/block.ts class Block, ~1.1k lines) is a DOM-like node: blockId, element (semantic tag), children[], baseStyles / mobileStyles / tabletStyles (camelCase CSS maps), attributes, customAttributes, classes[], innerHTML, dataKey + dynamicValues (bindings to page data), isRepeaterBlock, visibilityCondition, props (typed, with isStandard/isPassedDown/isDynamic/comesFrom), clientScript, extendedFromComponent + componentVersion + isChildOfComponent + referenceBlockId (component instances resolve their reference block through componentStore, pinned to a frozen version snapshot when set). Components are Builder Component docs; builder/builder/component_versions.py pins versions at drag-drop and pin_components_in_page_data() pins the rest at publish. RENDER/PUBLISH: builder_page.publish() sets published=1, staging=0, calls promote_draft_blocks() which take_snapshot()s draft_blocks + page_data_script (snapshot_type Publish, pruned to KEEP_PUBLISH_SNAPSHOTS), copies draft_blocks -> blocks, saves, and enqueues a preview image; publish_to_staging/mark_as_staging serve the route but disable indexing; restore_snapshot restores into the draft. get_context() (Frappe website generator hook) runs the page data script, picks draft_blocks in preview mode, and calls get_block_html(blocks) -> BeautifulSoup tree: per block extend_block_with_component(), process_block_props() (standard props stack, dynamic props become Jinja refs), build_tag() creates the tag with CSS classes emitted into one <style> (base + tablet/mobile media queries, font registration, italic tracking), render_repeater_children() for data-bound loops, attach_client_script(); the resulting HTML + style are rendered through Jinja against page data, then meta tags, favicon, language, fonts (Google font URLs or user fonts) and global/page client scripts are attached; on_update() clears route caches and, in developer mode, exports standard pages/templates to an app as files. EDITOR: Pinia stores (pageStore, canvasStore, componentStore, blockTemplateStore, builderStore); frontend/src/utils/useCanvasHistory.ts implements undo/redo with @vueuse watchIgnorable + debounceFilter(100 ms) on the root Block: each record is the serialized whole tree (getBlockString) + selected ids; CAPACITY 500 entries, MAX_BYTES 20 MB with MIN_ENTRIES 10, reference-counted pause()/resume() during drag/resize, batch(), silentSetSource() for snapshot preview without recording, enable/disable for read-only. AI AGENT (builder/ai/): agent/loop.py AgentRunner drives a litellm tool-calling loop (MAX_ROUNDS 40, stream retries, Anthropic cache markers on system/turn, FULL_CONTEXT_LIMIT 45k chars above which the page is sent as a compact outline and read_block pulls detail); the server-side WorkingTree (agent/tree.py) is authoritative: every block op is applied there first, persisted to draft_blocks after each round, and only accepted ops are mirrored to the canvas (a live view); ops are rejected with honest messages for bad refs, non-plain bind keys (BIND_KEY_RE), repeater-via-bind, and moustache/Jinja text in content (which would crash the published route). agent/registry.py: each Tool has a side 'client' (block ops), 'server' (handler returns text) or 'terminal' (ends turn: present_ui, request_confirmation), optionally an 'artifact' + generator (generate_page streams page YAML from a heavier model, page_writer.py expands YAML -> Block JSON with style normalization). block_codec.py compresses Block JSON to a compact YAML vocabulary (el, ref, name, style, m_style, t_style, attrs, text, c, classes, icon) so the model never sees raw SVG or editor fields. Tools: generate_page, add_block/update_block/update_blocks/remove_block/move_block, query_blocks/read_block(show_image), preview_page (screenshot at viewport/colour scheme), set_page_script/update_script, set_design_token, query_records, run_python, connect_form, search_images, read_url/research, present_ui, memory. agent/pending.py confirm-gates sensitive kinds (home_page, global_settings, create_doctype, seed_sample_data, connect_form): the tool persists a pending action and ends the turn; only the user's Apply runs it. snapshots.py saves a revert snapshot before any turn that uses SNAPSHOT_TOOLS so every AI turn is revertable. prompts.py encodes hard rules: style on blocks or Builder Tokens only (never :root CSS), tokens referenced by document id, colours are facts to be read not guessed, never invent facts about a real business (delegate to research/read_url), no emoji icons (Lucide), summaries may claim only what preview_page showed, banned self-praise words.
core_innovation: A server-authoritative working tree that validates and applies every AI block operation before mirroring it to the editor, combined with a lossy-but-round-trippable codec that shows the model a compact YAML view of the same block JSON the visual editor and server renderer use.
strengths: One block tree is the contract for editor (Vue Block class), server renderer (get_block_html via BeautifulSoup + one generated stylesheet), publish snapshots, and the AI agent (via BlockCodec); no second renderer, and published pages are lean static HTML that scores well on Lighthouse.

WorkingTree rejects invalid ops deterministically (bad ref, expression bind keys, moustache text, repeater misuse) and returns honest tool results, so the model self-corrects; canvas and server cannot diverge because only accepted ops are mirrored.
Confirm-gating (pending.py): sensitive writes are proposals persisted as pending actions and applied only by user action; every mutating turn gets a pre-turn revert snapshot.

Publish pipeline is a real state machine: draft_blocks vs blocks, staging vs published, Publish/Manual snapshots with pruning, component version pinning at drag-drop and at publish, route-cache invalidation on any relevant field change.
Component versioning: instances carry componentVersion and resolve against frozen version snapshots, so editing a component cannot silently change a published page.
Undo/redo is production-grade: debounced deep watcher, byte-capped stack, reference-counted pause for gestures, silent source swap for previewing snapshots.

Prompt rules that align with our philosophy: tokens are Builder Token records (never raw :root CSS), colours are read not guessed, facts about real businesses are never invented (research/read_url), summaries claim only what preview_page showed, self-praise vocabulary banned.
Context management: compact YAML codec, outline mode above 45k chars, Anthropic cache markers, streamed artifact from a heavier model separate from the conversational model.
Large test suite (builder_page tests 2k lines, ai/test_* for codec, tree apply, page writer, read_page, locks, web).
weaknesses: Element-level, Webflow-style model (div/section/h1 with camelCase style maps per breakpoint): no notion of section variants, arrangements, composition or archetypes; design quality is whatever the user or the model composes from raw CSS.

Hard dependency on Frappe Framework (bench, MariaDB/Postgres, Redis, Python website generator, Jinja): cannot be used inside an Astro/TS pipeline; the renderer emits HTML via BeautifulSoup + Jinja, not components.

The AI agent still lets the model author raw CSS values and layout (style maps in YAML) and search stock images; grounding is by prompt rules plus a few regex guards, not by a typed eligibility system.
Published output is one generated <style> block with generated class names; no design-token file surface comparable to our visual_dna, only Builder Token records referenced by uuid.
AI subsystem is new (2026) and coupled to Frappe realtime events, doctypes and Desk; loop.py is 1.5k lines with product-specific event contracts.
Snapshots serialise the whole tree per record (undo stack and publish snapshots), which the code itself notes gets heavy for large pages.
patterns_to_steal: Server-authoritative WorkingTree with op-level validation and mirror-only-accepted-ops -> Assembly and post-V1 editor: the canonical SiteDefinition lives in Postgres; model or editor proposals are ops validated by Zod + predicate rules server-side, and the UI only reflects accepted ops.

Deterministic op guards that encode 'this will crash the published page' knowledge (BIND_KEY_RE, MOUSTACHE_RE, repeater-via-bind) -> Anti-slop tier 1 / Launch QA: pure regex and structural bans on model output that cannot render (unknown variant ids, template syntax in copy, facts not in the FactRegistry).

BlockCodec: a compact, documented model-facing vocabulary generated from the same data model, with FIELD_DOCS as the single source for the prompt's field list -> agent orchestration: derive the model-visible catalogue of eligible ids/fields from the Zod schemas, never hand-type it.

Confirm-gated terminal tools (pending.py KINDS) -> orchestration: publish, positioning changes and anything owner-declared are proposals that end the turn and require explicit approval; the model can only propose.
Pre-turn revert snapshot for any mutating tool set -> Decision Manifest/telemetry: snapshot SiteDefinition before each pipeline stage so every change is revertable and diffable.

Publish state machine (draft vs published, staging, snapshot + prune, version pinning at publish, cache invalidation on field change) -> CMS/publish stage for Astro output: pin design_system and section library versions into the published manifest.
Outline-above-threshold context strategy (FULL_CONTEXT_LIMIT + read_block on demand) -> agent orchestration for large SiteDefinitions.

Prompt rules worth keeping as code checks: 'summary claims only what preview showed', 'never invent facts about a real business', 'colours are facts to be read' -> map to Launch QA screenshot verification, FactRegistry provenance and design-system token lookup.
patterns_to_avoid: Free-form element/CSS block model (element + style maps) -> we deliberately constrain to section variants x arrangements; letting the model author CSS values violates 'model selects, never emits a token'.
Frappe-coupled runtime (doctypes, Jinja website generator, realtime events) -> not portable to Astro/TS; take the mechanisms, not the code.
Stock-image search tool (search_images) as the imagery path -> our art direction requires real owner photos with asset constraints.
Whole-tree snapshot per undo record -> for large SiteDefinitions prefer op logs or structural sharing; keep the byte cap idea.
Prompt-only enforcement of design rules where a check is possible (e.g. 'no :root CSS') -> encode as validators.
reusable_patterns: AuthoritativeWorkingTree: apply proposed ops to a server-side model first, persist, then mirror only accepted ops to any live view.
ModelFacingCodec: a compact, documented projection of the canonical schema shown to the model, with the field list generated from one table.
ConfirmGatedTerminalTool: sensitive actions end the turn as persisted proposals that only a human can apply.
PreTurnRevertSnapshot: snapshot the artefact before any mutating tool set so a whole turn can be reverted.
DraftPublishStateMachine: draft/published/staging fields with snapshot-on-publish, pruning and dependency version pinning.
OutlineOnOverflow: send a structural outline above a size threshold and let the model fetch detail on demand.
adoption_strategy: Adapt. Do not run Frappe; the block model is element-level and the runtime is Python/Jinja. Port five mechanisms into TypeScript: the authoritative working-tree op pipeline (Zod + predicate validation before mirroring), deterministic 'this cannot render' guards into the anti-slop gate, a generated model-facing codec/catalogue derived from the Zod schemas, confirm-gated terminal tools plus pre-turn snapshots for the orchestration loop, and the draft/staging/publish state machine with version pinning for the publish stage. Its prompt rules about facts, colours and self-praise are a useful checklist to convert into code checks. This is the most architecturally mature repo in the category and the best reference for the post-V1 visual editor's undo and component-version design.
